subject: Tenant boundary and hosting confirmation for EU PoC
message_1_subject: Tenant isolation and EU-hosting confirmation for PoC
message_1_body:
Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Finteq is keen to move to a short PoC but our security team needs a short written confirmation around two items before we can approve network access: 

1) Physical/region residency: For the PoC we need to verify that all inference, logs and KV cache for the Finteq tenant will be confined to EU regions (specifically eu-west-1) and will not egress to the US for processing or backups.

2) Tenant boundary / VPC model: We need a clear statement of the deployment options you support for private customers: shared-hosting with logical tenancy, isolated VPC per customer, or a managed private-link model. If you support customer-provided VPCs with PrivateLink/Peering and customer KMS keys (bring-your-own-key), please confirm the flow and any limitations.

Can you provide a short written confirmation plus any artifacts (network diagram, region matrix, KMS usage notes) we can attach to our procurement security review?

Appreciate it — if easier we can hop on a 20-minute call this week.

Cheers,
Alex Morton
Security Lead, Finteq
[attachment: finteq-questionnaire.pdf (PDF)]

message_3_subject: Re: Fwd: Tenant isolation and EU-hosting confirmation for PoC
message_3_body:
Kimberly / Dylan — TL;DR: For a Private deployment we can provide tenant-level isolation and regional residency guarantees. Details below and attachments included.

Key points:
- Deployment modes supported for Private customers: 
  * Dedicated VPC per customer (recommended for Finteq PoC): full network boundary, no shared network plane.
  * PrivateLink / VPC Peering (managed): supports customer-managed connectivity; compute remains in the region you select.
  * Hosted-but-tenant-isolated (shared infra): logical tenancy with strict tenant separation at the application layer — this is not recommended for regulated customers.
- Region residency: For dedicated VPCs and Private deployments we can pin compute, storage (S3-like object store), and KV caches to eu-west-1. Backups and snapshots can be restricted to the same region; we do not replicate to other regions unless customer opt-in is configured at provisioning.
- KMS / keys: We support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) in supported clouds; keys remain in the customer's chosen region and are used for encrypting persistent storage and snapshots. Ephemeral in-memory caches are not written to disk.
- Operational notes & limitations:
  * Cross-region failover is optional and only triggered by customer-approved DR configuration.
  * Audit logs and control-plane telemetry may be accessible from our control plane — for Private deployments the control plane can be run in a customer VPC to avoid telemetry egress.

Attachments prepared:
- redwood-region-matrix.csv (lists services, storage, logs, KV and where they can be pinned)
- vpc-tenant-segmentation.pdf (diagram + notes)
- kms-usage-summary.txt (CLI snippet and key lifecycle notes)

If this looks good I can produce a short one-page confirmation letter we can sign and send.

— Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Inference Runtime
message_4_subject: Re: Tenant isolation and hosting confirmation for Finteq PoC — artifacts attached
message_4_body:
Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the requested artifacts and a short confirmation you can include in your procurement packet. High-level summary below; see attachments for specifics.

Summary (for procurement/security):
- Region residency: For a Private deployment in eu-west-1 we will ensure inference, persistent storage, and KV cache are provisioned and remain in eu-west-1. Backups/snapshots will be configured to remain in eu-west-1 unless explicit cross-region DR is requested and approved.
- Tenant boundary & VPC options:
  1) Dedicated VPC per customer (recommended): full network isolation; customer may provide VPC or we can provision one in their account.
  2) Customer-managed connectivity via AWS PrivateLink / VPC Peering: compute remains in the selected region; route controls are customer-managed.
  3) Shared-hosting with logical tenancy: supported for non-regulated workloads only.
- BYOK / KMS: Supported. Customer can supply a regional KMS key; keys never leave the region and are used for encrypting persistent artifacts.

Attached:
- redwood-region-matrix.csv (service residency matrix)
- vpc-tenant-segmentation.pdf (architecture diagram)
- kms-usage-summary.txt (short notes / CLI snippets)

Next steps: If you want, Marcus and I can join a 20-minute technical alignment to review the attachments and sign the confirmation. When would work for you this week?

Warm regards,
Kimberly Park
VP, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
